content_html_sanitized:
Posted May 25, 2001
(MarijuanaNews note: I had been wanting to run the second item for a few days, but now I am glad that I waited. It is wonderful how the Internet brings things together to create context.

The Dutch medical cannabis program is finally under way. That is nice for Dutch patients, but it is also very important because of its impact on the rest of the world. It will give the rest of Europe a nudge in the right direction. And not just Europe…

Health Canada is in the process of " finalizing " its medical cannabis program and is making it overly complicated while telling themselves and the world that this will be the first medical cannabis program. Wrong!

A friend was kind enough to send me this translation from an unidentified Dutch newspapers parliamentary report.)

Van onze parlementaire redactie:

The Netherlands First Production of 'Royal Hemp'
(MarijuanaNews note: " Royal Hemp " is the translation of " rijkshennep " – official cannabis, we might say, if we were so lucky!)

Health Minister Borst has received a shipment of medicinal cannabis from England. Since the founding of " Bureau for Medicinal Cannabis " the minister is allowed to grow medicinal cannabis for patients who suffer from painful diseases such as MS.
See
Dutch National Cannabis Agency To Be Launched
To Regulate Cannabis Production for Medical And Scientific Purposes
and
Two Press Releases from Swedish Prohibitionists Tell Us A Little About Dutch and Australian Policies – And Too Much About the Prohibitionist Mentality.

She let the government know that no suitable Dutch grower has been found to date. But today the first shipment arrived from England.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is ironic in several ways.

First, it is like " coals to Newcastle. "

There is a huge amount of cannabis – nederwiet – grown in Holland, but it is almost all illegal, so the government would have had to deal with people who are technically criminals. Instead, they decided to import it from the UK, where it is legally grown by GW Pharmaceuticals, which is going to go public soon with an estimated market capitalization [total number of shares owned by everyone times the offering price] of around $240 million.

Patients with serious illnesses can get a joint by prescription for 'royal hemp' in order to make their pain bearable.

Until now, these people had to go to a coffee shop, something that Health Minister Borst thought was unacceptable.
(MarijuanaNews note: In the rest of the world sick people would love to have that option!)
See
If marijuana has medical value, why isn't medically available in the Netherlands?
and
Belgium to Import Dutch Marijuana for Medical Tests to Expedite the Process, While the UK Government Says It Will Stall for Four More Years to Pharmaceuticalize Cannabis.
(MarijuanaNews note: Clearly the Belgians will also have to get it from England.)


(MarijuanaNews note: I am posting this in order to make some comments, but I urge you to visit the RN site to see the pictures and for some of the side bar pop-ups at .)

Nick deals in soft drugs. He works in The Grasshopper - one of Amsterdam's most famous ‘coffee shops'. A stone's throw from Central Station, on the edge of the red light district, it attracts an international crowd. Mostly tourists, looking to sample a little of what the city has to offer, preferably within stumbling distance of their hotel.

He's nervous about talking to me. This may be Amsterdam, but people in the ‘coffee shop' industry don't like to draw too much attention to themselves. After a drink and a cigarette, Nick begins to relax. " Basically I sell the grass and the hash here, " he tells me. He's been in The Netherlands for 21 years, but his accent gives away that originally he's from Manchester. How did he end up working in The Grasshopper? " I just walked in and asked the boss if they needed someone for the job. " He gives me a wry smile and adds, " actually, I always wanted to be a lawyer. "

No Rest

It seems a hedonistic lifestyle doesn't allow for lying in bed. Nick's day starts early. The doors open at 8 in the morning. " I had it so bad one time, quarter to eight they were waiting there already, trying to get in. " He'll sell you nine different types of weed, and nine types of hash. " All the weed we sell are locally grown, all the hash is imported. We've got some from Morocco. A couple from India. "
(MarijuanaNews note: See footnote 1 – below – on " weed. " )

He's also happy to give you help and advice. " People ask me questions all the time. One of the biggest questions is ‘what's the difference between weed and hash?' I tell them, weed is more of a happy kind of high. Hash is more of a stony kind of effect. "

Rules of the House

I'm curious to know where the supplies of drugs come from. Nick is giving nothing away. " Basically, I arrive in the morning and it's fully stocked up. " I press him a little more. He changes the subject. So instead we talk about the rules the coffee shop must follow if it wants to remain open and licensed.
See
Dutch Parliament Surprises Its Own Government -- Votes to " Legalize " Cultivation of Marijuana – By One Vote.

The maximum stock allowed on the premises is 500g. " You can't go over that - not one gram. " No-one under the age of 18 is allowed in the coffee shop, and this is enforced by checking ID. No alcohol is sold. And definitely no hard drugs.
(MarijuanaNews note: That link is to the Radio Netherlands web site side bar on hard drugs policies. The article notes with pride that " the number of drug related deaths in The Netherlands is the lowest in Europe…. Also, the population of hard-drug addicts does not grow, as particularly heroin does not appeal to the young. To them, heroin is a drug for losers. The group of heroin users has an average age of 41. " )
See
The Spin Is Beginning To Wobble On The " Latest Teen Drug Use " Survey. Czar Is " Greatly Encouraged " By Poll Showing Heroin Use By 12th Graders At All Time High.

Nick tells me they have regular inspections from the police. " At any given moment they could drop in, and at least five times a year. " But he is keen to stress that they have very good relations with the police " because we stick to the rules ".

Not All Bad

No surprises that Nick is a regular cannabis smoker himself. Perhaps more surprising is that he has asthma. " You've heard the expression ‘a joint a day keeps the doctor away?', well it works for me too. Since I started smoking weed, I've been taking less medicine. "
(MarijuanaNews note: See footnote 2 – below – on " medical cannabis. " )

So what does he think about the way he earns a living? " I love my job. For one it's original. OK, people might think ‘woah - he's dealing drugs'. But I only see positive things. "

And what about his future? He says he plans to stay in the coffee shop business at least for the next few years. " I'm having a swell time over here. " And what about his dreams of becoming a lawyer? " I'm keeping my hopes up. "

Foot notes
(1. Weed: It is estimated that more than half of marihuana sold in coffee shops is the homegrown Dutch variety, known as Nederwiet. Twenty years ago Nederwiet was considered to be of inferior quality. In those days, you might just as well have tried to get high on dried spinach. Since then, things have changed. After many years of crossing and cloning in garages, attics and balconies but above all in large professionally equipped greenhouses, it has a smooth taste and is quite potent. Nederwiet often has a higher THC-content than imported hemp (THC = delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol, the active ingredient in marihuana). The super-strong variety goes by the name of ‘skunk'. Each year about 100 tonnes of marihuana is grown in The Netherlands, of which more than half is exported.)

(2. Medical cannabis: Although there is an ongoing public debate about medical use of cannabis, its usefulness has been known for decades. Apparently the British queen, Victoria, used cannabis for period pains. In many cases it has been reported that cannabis helps to alleviate pain of MS patients, cancer and aids patients, counteracts negative side effects of medicines and is useful for sufferers from glaucoma. Although there is no conclusive scientific proof of the beneficial effects of cannabis, patient organizations and health care services argue strongly in favour of its application. The Dutch government has set up an official agency to supervise medical distribution of cannabis.)
